tasks.short: Run statistical analyses, simulations and network models.

steps.what: Prepare data for social network pattern analysis.
Choose network modeling, discrete event simulation or agent-based modeling.
Check diagnostics on the mathematical optimization.

tasks.design: Study data can be prepared on {DATA_PLATFORM}, and the statistical analyses run there once the engineer has chosen the method, including network modeling, discrete event simulation or agent-based modeling. Diagnostics are checked. Interpretation, including natural language processing, stays with the engineer, and the computational sociology result is filed only after that.
tasks.previous_blocker: Method, data and the write-up were separate files, and a failed run was still quoted.
tasks.enabler_now: Preparation and the run can be repeated. Choosing the method and reading the result stay.
tasks.still_hard: A run that finishes and answers a different question.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer will not file a result the diagnostics do not support.

ambition.what: Give the industrial engineer the same checked run, not only the human factors note.

tasks.altitude: Interpretation stays. The engineer can withhold a result the diagnostics failed.

reach.task: Reuse the same run for a line study
reach.learn: Which inputs the line study may share and which belong only to this question

evidence.claim: A calculation that runs is not the same as a result the engineer accepts.
A drafted number is usable only when it traces to a record the engineer accepts.
A decision about a worker may not be solely automated.

assumptions: Focal role is the human factors engineer. Boundary: from study data to a filed result. Collecting the data is out of scope.
Structured fields are method, input table, run id and diagnostic status. The study data produce the table. Fallback: a run that did not finish is not filed.
If the inputs are about identifiable workers, no solely automated decision about a worker is made from the run.
unknowns: Whether the data are about people who can be identified.
Which methods the question is allowed to use.
research_questions: Which results need a second method before they are filed?

already_counted.description: Choosing a method the question can support

incremental.description: Keep method names and run ids attached to the result

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Clean data and a known method save preparation and the run. Method choice and interpretation stay. The low case is a question the first method does not fit.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Forecast human decisions, behaviors and group actions.

steps.what: Define the structure of events in organizations.
Assemble modeling inputs on processes and groups.
Apply quantitative analysis to forecast the events.
Judge human decisions, behaviors and attitudes.
Explain group actions and the forecast.

tasks.design: Inputs on processes and groups can be assembled in {SPREADSHEET}, and a quantitative analysis can forecast the events on {DATA_PLATFORM}. The engineer defines the events, judges human decisions, behaviors and attitudes, and explains group actions in person. The forecast is not used as a decision about one worker.
tasks.previous_blocker: The model and the explanation were separate, and a stale run was briefed as current.
tasks.enabler_now: The run can be repeated when inputs change. The definition, the judgement and the explanation stay.
tasks.still_hard: A forecast that fits the numbers and misstates what the group can actually do.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer will not brief a forecast as a fact about a named person.

ambition.what: Refresh the forecast when new observations arrive, not once a year.

tasks.altitude: Explanation stays a conversation. The engineer can refuse to present a run the judgement did not accept.

reach.task: Say which group action would change a route choice
reach.learn: Which forecast outputs a route study can use and which are about something else

evidence.claim: A decision about a worker may not be solely automated.
Employment uses of such systems are treated as high-risk under the EU AI Act.
A calculation that runs is not the same as a result the engineer accepts.
Advice, design and research stay with the engineer; a draft is not the decision.

assumptions: Focal role is the human factors engineer. Boundary: from a forecast question to an explanation. Acting on the forecast is the decision maker's work.
Structured fields are event, group, input period and run id. Observations produce the inputs. Fallback: a run with missing inputs is not briefed.
No solely automated decision about a worker. The forecast is about groups and events, not a sanction.
unknowns: Whether observations are current enough to rerun.
research_questions: Which forecasts need new observations before they are explained?

already_counted.description: Judging a forecast the run cannot defend
Defining the event the question left vague

incremental.description: Keep event names and run ids on the explanation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Fresh observations save input assembly and the run. Defining the event, judging it and explaining it stay. The low case is a question with thin observations.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Runs and data preparation get shorter. Method choice and the forecast judgement stay.
reach: Transportation engineers reading a group-action forecast
skills_to_grow: Choosing a method the question can support
Refusing a forecast that would decide about one worker
Showing the inputs behind a run
role.ambitious_version: The industrial engineer sees the same checked run, and a forecast is refreshed when new observations arrive.
